title: Independent challenge of a project architecture
description: The second model's job in /idp-establish is the inverse of the architect's: it is given an architecture a human already wrote and asked to find what will not hold. Enforced the same way as reviewer.schema.json — by the provider's own output schema, and by this schema again when the fallback runs.

verdict.description: 'sound' means the challenger found nothing. It is allowed, and it is not the same as an empty findings list produced by a provider that failed — that failure is a mode, recorded separately.

kind.description: contradiction — two parts of the architecture cannot both be true. gap — something the architecture must say and does not. boundary — a responsibility sits in the wrong component.

components.description: Which components the finding is about. Empty when it is about the whole. Required and nullable rather than optional, because strict structured output has no other way to say optional (IDE-145).

claim.description: What will not hold, stated so that it can be argued with. 'The catalogue owns product data and the storefront writes it' is a claim; 'data ownership is unclear' is not.

severity.description: blocking — the architecture cannot carry the product until this is answered. material — it can, at a cost that must be recorded. minor — worth knowing, not worth stopping for.
